current.text: Utah's projected starting lineup is Keyonte George, Darryn Peterson, Lauri Markkanen, Jaren Jackson Jr. and Jusuf Nurkic.
He shares touches with Jaren Jackson Jr., who is there for a full season, rookie Darryn Peterson and Keyonte George. All of them are expected to lose some usage.
The experts expect him to produce less than last season. One projects 34 minutes and a 25 usage rate. Utah's scoring should be balanced, and no one is expected to reach a career high in points.
The Jazz are not tanking this season. They are trying to win.
The experts call the fear that Utah will tank or sit him misplaced. They say this fear is the main reason drafters mark him down.

Utah is projected around 43 wins and a 7th or 8th seed, with a top 10 offense and a defense ranked below 20th. The team probably makes the playoffs, so the late-season minutes of the tank years will not be there.
Minutes and usage on the Jazz are expected to be all over the place early in the season. Coach Will Hardy will feel pressure to tinker in order to win.
In category leagues he is worth a pick around 25 to 32. Pick 25 is early but acceptable. He should not go in the first round.
The experts call him underrated at a Yahoo ADP of 44. They call his ESPN ADP of 77 to 89 a steal.
In one auction mock he sold for 30 USD. The expert had hoped to get him for 21 to 22 USD.

durable.text: He is a scoring forward. His FT% is elite on real volume, and he adds many threes and points for a forward. His assists are low, and his steals and blocks are about average.
His best position is power forward. He has played out of position at small forward for the last couple of years.
For years he has played several short stints per game. He comes out early and then goes back in.
He has missed many games in his career. Some were real injuries and some were tank-driven holdouts.
The experts disagree on his health. One says he cannot stay healthy. Others call his injury concerns mostly exaggerated.
He is worth more in category leagues than in points leagues. In points leagues the experts call him a fourth-round player, around pick 40 to 50.

note: Markkanen is a scoring forward. His FT% is elite on volume, he hits about 3 threes a game and adds strong points. No category is weak enough to rule him out of any build. Yahoo values him at 29 USD against a 21.4 USD average cost, while ESPN has him at 20 USD and 13.9 USD, and he went for 16 USD in our league last year. A bid in the mid-20s fits the experts' round-3 grade, but one mock already reached 30 USD. Early in the season, check how much usage he keeps next to Jaren Jackson Jr. and Darryn Peterson, and whether he stays healthy after playing only 42 games.
